result.notes:
HARNESS COMPLIANCE 5/5: (1) research-gate-before-contract -- research_brief mtime 11:28:38 < contract 11:32:29; envelope gate_passed=true, 5 read-in-full, 18 snippet-only, 23 URLs, 17 internal files, dedicated "Recency scan (2024-2026)" section at line 191. (2) contract-before-generate -- contract 11:32:29 < corpus 11:35:00 < test file 11:39:55 < fetcher.py 11:40:43. (3) experiment_results + live_check present (11:42:45 / 11:42:08), both after the last code edit. (4) log-last -- no "## Cycle ... phase=83.0.1" header in harness_log; masterplan 83.0.1 still status=pending. (5) no-verdict-shopping -- cycle 1, no evaluator_critique for 83.0.1, 0 CONDITIONAL entries, retry_count=0 (certified_fallback false).

PER-CRITERION (all MET):
C1 MET -- test asserts the VALUE (row["published_at"] is None) + strict counter increase (after == before+1) + serializer NULL, not merely "a counter exists". Persisted half proven live: my own query returns article_id 65a9abd5... with published_at None, 1 NULL row visible without a partition predicate. Non-vacuous: my qa4 (bq_writer coerces NULL to a value) kills exactly this test.
C2 MET -- I reproduced the named mutant TWO ways: faithful source-level restore of `or _now_iso()` at the published_at= field (5 failed) and a semantic restore at the parse seam (10 failed). BOTH fail test_c1_missing_published_at_yields_null_and_quarantines, which is what the criterion requires. The author reported 4 failed; the fallback can be restored at two placements and the count is construction-dependent while the kill of the C1 test is invariant -- kill counts are scope-dependent, named tests are the invariant. No finding.
C3 MET and non-vacuous -- my independent mutant qa1 (ingested_at=(published_at or _now_iso()), literally "written as the article's own era") produced exactly 1 failure: test_c3_backfill_ingested_at_never_earlier_than_published_at. NAMED KILL MECHANISM (shape #11 discipline): `assert ing >= pub` does NOT kill it (equality passes); the killer is `assert ing.year >= 2026`. The author's inline comment correctly calls that "the sharp half".
C4 MET -- derived (RuleA date_to_session(pub+_EMBARGO_DAYS, "next")) and persisted (verified live: effective_trade_date=2022-03-16 on the 2022-03-15 backfill row; column DATE NULLABLE in my own schema read). Corpus test asserts n_sessions>=1 AND RuleA exactness ==1 so over-embargo also fails. qa2 (same-day date) kills 4 tests including both C4 tests.
C5 MET -- _EMBARGO_DAYS=0 produces exactly 3 failures, reproducing the author's "3 failed": C4 corpus, C4 entry-open, C1 negative control.
C6 MET -- no threshold assertion; the only assert is an internal-consistency identity (quarantine_count == loop count). I reproduced the emitted record: "QUARANTINE RECORDED: 4 of 13 corpus articles (matches loop count 4)".

FINDINGS (NOTE-level, none a criterion miss, none BLOCK/WARN):
F1 MIS-ATTRIBUTED KILL MECHANISM (vacuity shape #11, qa.md 4b). experiment_results.md line 30 states m2 is caught by "the intraday-weekday fixture ... a weekend-only corpus would survive". Does NOT reproduce. Under the full corpus the assert that actually trips is verbatim `AssertionError: backfill_2022: only 0 sessions in (2022-03-15, 2022-03-15]`. And my fixture mutant qa6 (corpus 13->10, removing intraday_weekday + backfill_2022 + no_ticker_macro, THEN embargo=0) still yields 3 failures -- the `friday` article (2022-06-10) also produces a zero-session window, and two hardcoded in-test articles (test_c1_negative_control expecting eff=="2022-06-09" and test_c4_entry_price) kill it independently. The guard is STRONGER than claimed, so this is a claim-accuracy note, not a criterion miss; but the stated rationale would misdirect a future maintainer pruning fixtures.
F2 LATENT CONSUMER OF THE NULLABLE WIDENING. backend/news/dedup.py:98 filters `WHERE published_at >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL @days DAY)`, so NULL-published rows evaluate NULL>=X and fall outside the cross-batch dedup window -- the SAME __NULL__-partition trap the contract documents for its own live_check query, now present in production SQL. Consequence if wired: a persistently-broken vendor feed re-inserts every quarantined article on every run (canonical_url/body_hash are still computed for quarantined rows). DORMANT TODAY: the only call site is dedup.py:159 in the module's own _smoke() with bq_client=None; grep found no production caller, so there is no live impact. Recommend queueing as its own step per the standing "queue discovered defects in the masterplan" rule. Undisclosed in contract/experiment_results.
F3 FIXTURE ONLY WEAKLY PINNED. My qa5 (corpus 13->10, no code mutation) passes 15/15 -- the corpus is pinned only by `len(articles) >= 10` plus `min(deltas)==1 and max(deltas)>=2`, and BOTH survive removing every delta-1 weekday/backfill case because sunday/MLK/July-4 also yield delta 1. Not a criterion miss (qa6 proves the C5 kill does not depend on the removable part), but the corpus could be silently thinned; recommend pinning by case-name.
F4 C6 RECORD IS WRITE-ONLY. pytest default capture suppresses the QUARANTINE RECORDED line under the immutable `-q` command, and "4 of 13" appears in NO handoff artifact. The criterion's literal requirement (recorded, not thresholded) is met by the mechanism; recommend quoting the number in experiment_results.md so an operator reading the artifact sees it.
F5 GUARD-PLACEMENT + SCOPE NOTES. (a) my qa3 (bq_writer stops emitting effective_trade_date) SURVIVES the immutable command's suite (15 passed) but is KILLED by backend/tests/test_bq_writer.py (2 failed) -- the persistence seam is guarded, just outside the immutable command's file; combined with the live row, C4's "persisted" half is genuinely covered. (b) C4's OPEN-vs-CLOSE half is a TEST-LOCAL simulation: grep confirms effective_trade_date has no consumer outside fetcher/bq_writer/migration, so no production code chooses the entry anchor yet. The criterion's own wording ("the fixture's SIMULATED entry price") anticipates this, so it is met as written -- recorded so a later step does not assume the anchor is enforced on a pricing path.

D5 TOMBSTONE CLEARED (checked for criteria-erosion, rejected): `git show --stat 06911cb5 -- backend/news/sources/finnhub.py backend/news/sources/benzinga.py` is genuinely EMPTY, so 83.0's byte-unchanged criterion was discharged at that commit and git history preserves it permanently. The retired test asserted working-tree `git diff HEAD` emptiness FOREVER over those paths -- structurally uncloseable once any later step legitimately touched them (the immutable-criteria-must-be-green-able class). Disclosed in contract D5 pre-generate, tombstoned in-file, and the tombstone explicitly declines to pretend a replacement covers it. Not silent, not erosion.

CLAIM AUDIT (4b) -- reproduced by me: "15 passed in 2.21s" (got 2.22s); "46 passed" (exact); lint "All checks passed!" over my own derived scope; the live ALTER schema; the backfill row and __NULL__ row byte-for-byte; "06911cb5 empty diff"; "4 of 13" quarantine; "2 source='fixture' rows added" pollution (exactly 2 fixture rows present). Not reproduced: the m2 mechanism attribution (F1). Construction-dependent: m1 "4 failed" / m5 "5 failed" (my differently-built mutants gave 5 and 7; kills invariant).

CODE-REVIEW HEURISTICS: no BLOCK, no WARN. bq-schema-migration-safety is the SAFE direction (DROP NOT NULL relaxation + NULLABLE ADD COLUMN, no drop, research-cited vendor semantics, one-way and disclosed). The broad `except Exception` in _derive_effective_trade_date LOGS and fails CLOSED into quarantine -- correct for an embargo and explicitly contrasted in the contract with markets.is_trading_day's fail-open, so it is not the silences-a-risk-guard shape. Test-file "test-key"/_FakeSecret are fixtures (negation list). No execution-path, kill-switch, stop-loss, or perf-metrics surface touched. Loggers ASCII. No frontend files in the diff (1b N/A); no UI claims (1c N/A).

UNINTENDED CHANGE: none. All 9 changed .py files map to contract D1/D2/D5 scope; the remaining git-status entries are handoff artifacts, hook-written audit JSONLs, and researcher memory.
